description: The Common Operational Datasets are OCHA's agreed reference datasets for humanitarian response, so that all responders use the same administrative boundaries, place codes and baseline figures. They come in four types, administrative boundaries (COD-AB), edge-matched boundaries (COD-EM), population statistics (COD-PS) and country-specific datasets (COD-CS), keyed by P-codes and rated as Enhanced or Standard quality country by country; the COD Global Information Dashboard, built in Power BI, tracks their status country by country. They are maintained by OCHA with national authorities and partners. The datasets are available free through the Humanitarian Data Exchange and live geoservices; no single licence is stated on the dashboard page, and each HDX dataset carries its own. Caveats: a notice on the page, updated 21 February 2025, says the COD-AB workflow run with ITOS is being revised following US foreign aid cuts, and quality varies by country. They provide the boundary and population backbone for multi-sector exposure and emergency response models; a related record is the Humanitarian Data Exchange.
